questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary objective of accounting?
options: To record, classify and summarise financial transactions to determine results and position
To advertise products to customers
To manufacture goods at the lowest possible cost
To recruit employees for a firm
questions.explanation: Accounting's core purpose is systematically recording, classifying and summarising monetary transactions to ascertain profit/loss and financial position.

questions.text: A company prepares its financial statements assuming it will continue its operations for the foreseeable future and has no plan to liquidate its assets. Which accounting concept is being applied?
options: Going Concern concept
Money Measurement concept
Consistency concept
Conservatism concept
questions.explanation: The going concern concept assumes indefinite continuity of the business, which justifies valuing assets at cost rather than at forced-sale/liquidation value.

questions.text: When goods are purchased for cash, which journal entry correctly records the transaction?
options: Purchases A/c Dr., To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr., To Purchases A/c
Sales A/c Dr., To Cash A/c
Cash A/c Dr., To Sales A/c
questions.explanation: Purchases (an expense/asset-in-trade) increase and are debited, while Cash, an asset, decreases and is credited in a cash purchase transaction.

questions.text: A firm's cash book (bank column) shows a higher balance than its passbook on a given date, with no errors involved. Which of the following best explains this?
options: Cheques deposited by the firm but not yet collected/cleared by the bank
Cheques issued by the firm but not yet presented for payment
Bank charges debited by the bank but not yet recorded in the cash book
Interest credited by the bank but not yet recorded in the cash book
questions.explanation: Cheques deposited are debited (added) in the cash book as soon as they are deposited, but the bank credits the account only once the cheque is actually collected, so the cash book temporarily shows a higher balance than the passbook.

questions.text: Which type of error will NOT be detected by preparing a trial balance?
options: Complete omission of a transaction from both the accounts it should affect
Posting an entry to the wrong side of an account
Writing a wrong amount in only one of the two accounts affected
Omitting to post one side of a journal entry
questions.explanation: A complete omission affects neither the debit nor the credit side of the books, so the trial balance still balances; the other errors create a one-sided mismatch that the trial balance would reveal.
questions.topic: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors

questions.text: A machine is purchased for ₹2,00,000. Depreciation is charged at 10% per annum under the Written Down Value (Diminishing Balance) method. What is the book value of the machine at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: Under the WDV method, depreciation is calculated on the reducing balance each year: ₹2,00,000 becomes ₹1,80,000 after year 1 (10% deducted), and ₹1,80,000 becomes ₹1,62,000 after year 2 (10% of ₹1,80,000 deducted).

questions.text: In a bill of exchange, the person directed to pay the specified amount is called the:
options: Drawee
Drawer
Payee
Endorser
questions.explanation: The drawee is the party ordered by the drawer to pay the stated sum on the bill, and is typically the debtor who accepts the bill of exchange.

questions.text: The Trading Account of a business is prepared mainly to ascertain:
options: Gross profit or gross loss
Net profit or net loss
The overall financial position of the business
The amount of capital introduced by the owner
questions.explanation: The Trading Account matches sales revenue against the cost of goods sold to determine the gross profit or gross loss for the period.

questions.text: Which of the following is a distinguishing feature of 'commerce' as compared with 'industry'?
options: Commerce deals with the distribution and exchange of goods and services
Commerce deals only with the extraction of raw materials
Commerce deals only with manufacturing processes
Commerce refers exclusively to international trade
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade and auxiliary activities (banking, transport, insurance, etc.) that facilitate the distribution and exchange of goods, which is distinct from industry, concerned with production.

questions.text: In a partnership firm, what is the nature of the partners' liability for the firm's debts, unless otherwise agreed?
options: Unlimited and joint liability
Limited strictly to the amount of capital invested
No liability at all
Liability limited to profits earned that year
questions.explanation: Partners generally bear unlimited, joint liability for the firm's debts, meaning their personal assets can be used to settle business obligations if firm assets fall short.

questions.text: A statutory corporation such as the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) is established by:
options: A special Act of Parliament or State Legislature
Registration under the Companies Act
A partnership deed
A memorandum of association alone
questions.explanation: Statutory corporations are created through a special Act of the legislature, which defines their powers and functioning, unlike companies that are registered under the Companies Act.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a business service rather than a physical good?
options: Banking
Furniture
Wheat
Cement
questions.explanation: Banking is an intangible activity that facilitates business and commerce, whereas furniture, wheat and cement are tangible physical goods.

questions.text: Business ethics primarily refers to:
options: The application of moral principles of right and wrong to business conduct and decision-making
The legal minimum wage a firm must pay its employees
The accounting standards used for reporting profits
The advertising budget set aside by a company
questions.explanation: Business ethics concerns applying standards of honesty, fairness and transparency to business behaviour, going beyond mere legal compliance.
questions.topic: Social Responsibilities of Business and Business Ethics

questions.text: Retained earnings (ploughed-back profits) are considered a source of business finance that is:
options: Internal to the business
External and borrowed
Available only to sole proprietorships
A short-term liability like trade credit
questions.explanation: Retained earnings are generated from within the business itself, making them an internal source of long-term finance, unlike borrowed external funds.

questions.text: A 'chain store' (multiple shop organisation) in internal trade is best described as:
options: A number of retail outlets under common ownership, selling similar merchandise, located in different areas
A single large wholesale warehouse serving multiple independent retailers
A cooperative of independent retailers sharing only a common brand name
A door-to-door selling arrangement with no fixed outlet
questions.explanation: Chain/multiple shops are several retail branches owned and centrally controlled by one organisation, offering standardised merchandise and pricing across locations.

questions.text: A 'Letter of Credit' used in international trade primarily serves to:
options: Assure the exporter of payment, since the importer's bank guarantees payment on presentation of the specified documents
Insure the goods against loss or damage during transit
Grant the importer exemption from customs duty
Register the exporting firm's trademark abroad
questions.explanation: A Letter of Credit is issued by the importer's bank, assuring the exporter of payment once the required shipping documents are presented, which reduces payment risk in cross-border trade.

questions.text: At the time of India's independence, which sector employed the largest proportion of the workforce?
options: Agriculture
Manufacturing industry
Information technology services
Banking and finance
questions.explanation: Around 1947, agriculture was the predominant occupation, employing roughly 70-75% of the workforce, while industry and services remained relatively undeveloped.
questions.topic: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence

questions.text: India's industrial policy regime between 1950 and 1990, which required government permission before setting up or expanding industrial units, is commonly known as:
options: The Licence (Permit) Raj
The Green Revolution policy
The laissez-faire policy
The Zamindari system
questions.explanation: Under the Licence Raj, private firms needed government licenses to establish, expand or diversify production, reflecting the heavy regulation of industry during this period.

questions.text: 'Disinvestment', as part of India's privatisation policy, refers to:
options: The sale of a part of the government's equity/shareholding in public sector undertakings
The government's complete withdrawal of all subsidies to farmers
A complete ban on foreign direct investment
The nationalisation of private banks
questions.explanation: Disinvestment means the government sells off a portion of its equity holding in public sector enterprises, often to improve efficiency and raise resources.

questions.text: The 'poverty line' in India is typically defined on the basis of:
options: A minimum level of income or consumption expenditure needed to meet basic needs
The average income of the richest 10% of the population
The number of millionaires in a state
The total GDP of the country
questions.explanation: The poverty line is a benchmark expenditure/income level considered necessary to satisfy a minimum standard of living, covering food and non-food requirements.

questions.text: Investment in education and health is referred to as investment in 'human capital' primarily because it:
options: Improves the productive capacities and skills of people, much as physical capital raises output
Only benefits the government's tax revenue
Has no measurable impact on economic growth
Is accounted for in the same way as foreign direct investment
questions.explanation: Education and health raise individuals' productivity and capabilities, functioning like capital that increases future output, which is why it is termed human capital formation.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key focus area of rural development in India?
options: Diversification of rural livelihoods, sustainable agriculture, and access to credit in rural areas
Expansion of stock exchanges in metropolitan cities
Reduction in the number of commercial banks nationwide
Promotion of heavy luxury-goods manufacturing
questions.explanation: Rural development emphasises improving agricultural productivity, diversifying livelihoods, and ensuring access to credit, infrastructure and markets for the rural population.

questions.text: Workers in the 'informal sector' of the Indian economy are characterised mainly by:
options: Lack of job security, social security benefits and regulation under labour laws
Guaranteed pension and provident fund benefits
Fixed working hours strictly set by statute
Mandatory annual bonuses under the Factories Act
questions.explanation: Informal sector workers typically lack formal contracts, job security and statutory benefits such as provident fund or health insurance, unlike those in the organised/formal sector.
questions.topic: Employment: Growth, Informalisation and Other Issues

questions.text: 'Sustainable development' is best defined as development that:
options: Meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Maximises short-term industrial output regardless of resource depletion
Focuses exclusively on the GDP growth rate
Prohibits any use of natural resources whatsoever
questions.explanation: Sustainable development, as popularised by the Brundtland Report, balances current economic needs with preserving resources and environment for future generations.

questions.text: In economics, statistics is primarily used as a tool to:
options: Collect, organise, analyse and interpret numerical data to help understand economic phenomena
Predict the weather
Determine eligibility criteria for government jobs
Draft laws in parliament
questions.explanation: Statistics provides methods to systematically collect, present and analyse quantitative data, supporting economic analysis and decision-making.

questions.text: When data is collected directly by the investigator through personal interviews or surveys for a specific study, it is called:
options: Primary data
Secondary data
Published data
Census data, by definition
questions.explanation: Primary data is collected firsthand by the investigator for the specific purpose of the study, as opposed to secondary data, which is sourced from existing records compiled by someone else.

questions.text: A 'frequency distribution' organises raw data by:
options: Grouping values into classes and showing the number of observations in each class
Listing data purely in alphabetical order
Converting every value into a percentage of GDP
Removing all values below the median
questions.explanation: A frequency distribution arranges data into class intervals and records how many observations (frequency) fall into each, making large datasets easier to interpret.

questions.text: Which of the following is a graphical method of presenting statistical data?
options: Histogram
Mean
Standard deviation
Correlation coefficient
questions.explanation: A histogram is a diagrammatic tool used to visually present a frequency distribution, unlike the mean, standard deviation or correlation coefficient, which are numerical summary measures.

questions.text: The median of a data set is defined as:
options: The middle value when the data is arranged in ascending or descending order
The value that occurs most frequently in the data set
The sum of all values divided by the number of values
The difference between the highest and lowest values
questions.explanation: The median is the positional middle value of an ordered dataset, dividing it into two equal halves, unlike the mean (average) or mode (most frequent value).

questions.text: Which measure of dispersion uses ALL the values in a data set and is the most commonly used in statistical analysis?
options: Standard deviation
Range
Quartile deviation
Mode
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is calculated using every observation's deviation from the mean, making it a comprehensive and widely-used measure of dispersion, unlike range, which uses only the two extreme values.

questions.text: A correlation coefficient of -0.9 between two variables indicates:
options: A strong negative (inverse) linear relationship between the variables
A strong positive relationship between the variables
No relationship between the variables
That one variable definitely causes the other to change
questions.explanation: A coefficient close to -1 indicates a strong inverse relationship — as one variable increases, the other tends to decrease — though correlation alone does not establish causation.

questions.text: A price index number such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI) is primarily used to measure:
options: The relative change in the price level of a basket of goods and services over time, compared to a base period
The absolute quantity of goods produced in a year
The total population of a country
The exchange rate between two currencies
questions.explanation: Index numbers like the CPI express the percentage change in prices of a representative basket of goods relative to a fixed base period, and are commonly used to track inflation.

questions.text: Identify the type of sentence: "Although it was raining, the match continued."
options: Complex sentence
Simple sentence
Compound sentence
Interrogative sentence
questions.explanation: The sentence contains one independent clause ("the match continued") and one dependent clause introduced by "although," which is the structure of a complex sentence.
questions.topic: Advanced Grammar — Clauses and Sentence Types

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains a noun clause?
options: I know that she will come tomorrow.
The man who lives next door is a doctor.
She sang while the band played.
He arrived late, but nobody noticed.
questions.explanation: "That she will come tomorrow" functions as the object of the verb "know," which is the role a noun clause plays; the other sentences contain an adjective clause, an adverb clause, or two independent clauses joined by a conjunction.
questions.topic: Advanced Grammar — Clauses and Sentence Types

questions.text: The primary purpose of note-making while reading a passage is to:
options: Record the main ideas and key points in a brief, organised form for later reference
Rewrite the entire passage word for word
Add imaginative details not found in the original text
Translate the passage into another language
questions.explanation: Note-making condenses a text into its essential ideas using headings, sub-points and abbreviations, making it easier to revise and recall the information later.

questions.text: A good summary of a passage should:
options: Retain only the main ideas in the summariser's own words and omit minor details
Be longer than the original passage
Copy entire sentences verbatim from the original text
Include the summariser's personal opinions
questions.explanation: Summarising involves condensing the original text into fewer words while preserving its core meaning in one's own words, without adding opinions or unnecessary detail.

questions.text: A newspaper report, unlike a feature article, is primarily expected to:
options: Present factual information about an event in a clear, objective and chronological manner
Express the writer's personal feelings in an informal tone
Use poetic and highly figurative language
Be addressed directly to a single named recipient
questions.explanation: Reports are factual accounts of events, typically answering the key questions of who, what, when, where and why objectively, unlike the more subjective or narrative style of article writing.

questions.text: Which salutation would be most appropriate in a FORMAL letter addressed to the Editor of a newspaper?
options: Sir/Madam,
Hi there,
Dear Buddy,
Hey Editor,
questions.explanation: Formal letters use respectful, impersonal salutations such as "Sir/Madam," whereas casual greetings are appropriate only for informal correspondence.

questions.text: In a formal letter of complaint, which element is essential but is typically absent from an informal letter?
options: A clear, polite statement of the problem along with a specific request for redressal
Casual family news
Nicknames and inside jokes
Emoji and abbreviated text-speak
questions.explanation: A formal complaint letter must state the issue precisely and request specific action or redressal in a polite, structured tone, unlike an informal letter, which may simply share personal news.

questions.text: When answering comprehension questions based on a given passage, the most reliable strategy is to:
options: Base answers strictly on the information given in the passage rather than on prior personal knowledge
Answer purely from memory without referring back to the passage
Guess the answer based on the title alone
Write the longest possible answer regardless of relevance
questions.explanation: Comprehension answers should be derived from and supported by the given text, since the exercise tests understanding of that specific passage, not general knowledge.

questions.text: In 'The Portrait of a Lady' by Khushwant Singh, how does the author's relationship with his grandmother change after he goes abroad to study?
options: She grows distant and largely stops communicating or praying aloud with him as she used to
She writes him long emotional letters every single day
She travels abroad to visit him in person
Their relationship becomes closer than it had ever been
questions.explanation: After the narrator moves to the city and later abroad, his grandmother gradually withdraws and communicates with him far less than before, reflecting a growing emotional distance.

questions.text: In 'We Are Not Afraid to Die... if We Can All Be Together,' what major hazard does the crew of the Wavewalker face in the Pacific Ocean?
options: A huge wave capsizes the yacht during a violent storm
They run out of fuel near the coast
They are attacked by pirates
They lose radio contact in calm weather
questions.explanation: The narrator recounts how a massive wave capsized the yacht during a storm in the Pacific, badly damaging it and forcing the crew to fight for survival and make repairs.
questions.topic: We are Not Afraid to Die

questions.text: What modern investigative technique is described in 'Discovering Tut: The Saga Continues' for studying Tutankhamun's mummy without damaging it?
options: CT scanning
Carbon dating of pottery shards
X-ray crystallography of jewellery
DNA testing of the pyramid walls
questions.explanation: The chapter describes how a CT scan was used on Tutankhamun's mummy to study his remains non-invasively and investigate theories about the cause of his death.

questions.text: According to 'Landscape of the Soul,' how does traditional Chinese painting differ from traditional Western art in representing reality?
options: Chinese art aims to capture the inner spirit or essence of a subject rather than its exact physical likeness
Chinese art focuses only on photographic accuracy
Western art never attempts any form of realism
Chinese art uses no brushwork techniques at all
questions.explanation: The essay contrasts the Western pursuit of outer, literal likeness with the Chinese tradition's focus on conveying the inner essence of the subject, illustrated through anecdotes such as the painter and the butcher.

questions.text: Which international event/agreement is discussed in 'The Ailing Planet' in relation to global cooperation on environmental protection?
options: The Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro
The Treaty of Versailles
The Kyoto Protocol on trade tariffs
The Geneva Convention on armed conflict
questions.explanation: The chapter discusses the 1992 Rio 'Earth Summit' as a key global effort bringing nations together to address environmental degradation and promote sustainable development.
questions.topic: The Ailing Planet: The Green Movement's Role

questions.text: In 'The Browning Version,' what gift does the student Taplow give to his unpopular teacher, Mr. Crocker-Harris?
options: A second-hand copy of Robert Browning's verse translation of Agamemnon
A box of chocolates
A ticket to a cricket match
A pair of reading glasses
questions.explanation: Taplow gifts his teacher a used copy of Browning's translation of Agamemnon, a gesture of genuine affection that deeply moves the otherwise stern and unpopular teacher.

questions.text: Jayant Narlikar's 'The Adventure' explores an alternate version of history built around which scientific idea?
options: Catastrophe theory combined with a parallel-universe interpretation of events
The effect of relativity on gravity alone
The chemical composition of stars
The process of photosynthesis in plants
questions.explanation: The story uses catastrophe theory and the notion of parallel universes to imagine an alternate history in which a historical battle's outcome was different, framed as science fiction.

questions.text: In 'Silk Road,' what is the primary purpose of the narrator's journey toward Mount Kailash?
options: A pilgrimage and trek along part of the ancient trade route connecting Nepal and Tibet
A business trip to trade silk
A scientific expedition to study glaciers
A diplomatic mission to Lhasa
questions.explanation: The author recounts travelling as a pilgrim-trekker along part of the historic Silk Road toward Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, describing the physical challenges and cultural experiences of the journey.

questions.text: In 'The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse,' why do Mourad and Aram return the stolen horse after riding it for weeks?
options: Once its owner, John Byro, notices it, the boys feel compelled to return it out of their family's inherent honesty
The horse becomes too old to ride any further
The police track them down and force them to
They sell the horse for money instead
questions.explanation: Despite being poor, the boys' family values honesty above all; once the horse's owner recognises it, the boys quietly return it, reflecting this inherited trait.
questions.topic: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse

questions.text: In 'The Address' by Marga Minco, why is the narrator disappointed when she visits Mrs. Dorling's house after the war?
options: She recognises her family's belongings but feels the warmth and meaning of home are gone
The house has been completely demolished
Mrs. Dorling refuses to open the door at all
She discovers the address given to her was entirely wrong
questions.explanation: Although she recognises her mother's possessions in Mrs. Dorling's home, the narrator feels they have lost their original meaning and warmth, and she ultimately leaves without reclaiming them.

questions.text: In 'Ranga's Marriage,' what role does the narrator, Shyama, play in arranging Ranga's marriage to Ratna?
options: He stages a clever palm-reading trick to make Ranga believe fate has chosen Ratna for him
He forces Ranga into the marriage against his will through threats
He arranges the marriage through a government official
He has no involvement at all in the matchmaking
questions.explanation: Shyama uses a fabricated palmistry trick, pretending to read Ranga's future, to nudge the reluctant, English-educated Ranga toward accepting Ratna as his bride.

questions.text: According to the extract 'Albert Einstein at School,' what is Einstein's attitude toward the rigid, rote-learning style of his German school?
options: He is critical of it, feeling it suppresses independent and creative thinking
He fully supports and excels within the system
He has no opinion about the school system at all
He believes military-style discipline improves learning
questions.explanation: The extract portrays Einstein's discomfort with the authoritarian, fact-cramming education system, foreshadowing his lifelong preference for independent, imaginative thought over rote discipline.

questions.text: In J.B. Priestley's 'Mother's Day,' what change does Mrs. Pearson undergo after magically swapping places with her daughter Doris?
options: She becomes assertive and starts demanding respect and help from her family instead of being taken for granted
She becomes even more submissive than before
She decides to leave the family permanently
She loses her memory entirely
questions.explanation: While inhabiting her daughter's persona through Mrs. Fitzgerald's charm, Mrs. Pearson experiences life without being overworked and underappreciated, and resolves to assert herself and insist her family share household responsibilities.

questions.text: In 'The Ghat of the Only World,' what does the narrator primarily recall about his friend, the poet Agha Shahid Ali?
options: Shahid's courage, humour and poetic spirit while facing terminal illness
Shahid's career as a professional athlete
Shahid's role as a political leader in Kashmir's government
Shahid's refusal to ever discuss poetry
questions.explanation: The essay is a tribute recalling Agha Shahid Ali's warmth, wit and poetic sensibility during his final months battling illness, highlighting his remarkable composure and love of life.
questions.topic: The Ghat of the Only World

questions.text: In A.J. Cronin's 'Birth,' what critical complication does the young doctor face during the delivery?
options: The newborn appears stillborn, and he must try to resuscitate it against the odds
The mother refuses to be treated by a male doctor
The hospital runs out of essential medicine
Twins are born unexpectedly
questions.explanation: The story centres on the doctor's desperate, ultimately successful attempt to revive a baby who initially shows no signs of life at birth, testing his skill and resolve as a new physician.

questions.text: In Vikram Seth's poem 'The Tale of Melon City,' what absurd outcome results from the king's rule that whoever the fallen gate-arch strikes must be hanged?
options: The arch eventually falls on the king himself, and the tale ends with a melon being 'crowned' as the new ruler
The city is completely destroyed by the falling arch
The architect is rewarded with great riches
No one is ever found guilty under the rule
questions.explanation: The poem satirises arbitrary justice: after the arch falls on the king and the situation grows increasingly absurd, the story ends with a melon being 'crowned' king, mocking blind rule-following.

questions.text: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}, what is A ∩ B (A intersection B)?
options: { } (the empty set)
questions.explanation: The intersection of two sets contains only the elements common to both; here 2 and 3 appear in both A and B.

questions.text: A relation f from set A to set B is called a function if:
options: Every element of A is associated with exactly one element of B
Every element of B is associated with exactly one element of A
Some elements of A have no image in B
An element of A can map to multiple elements of B
questions.explanation: By definition, a function assigns to each element of the domain A exactly one element of the codomain B — no element of A is left unmapped or mapped to more than one output.

questions.text: In an Arithmetic Progression (AP) with first term a = 3 and common difference d = 4, what is the 5th term?
questions.explanation: The nth term of an AP is given by a + (n-1)d; substituting a = 3, d = 4, n = 5 gives 3 + 4(4) = 19.

questions.text: What is the value of sin(30°) + cos(60°)?
questions.explanation: sin 30° = 1/2 and cos 60° = 1/2, so their sum equals 1.

questions.text: What are the roots of the quadratic equation x² + 4 = 0 (in terms of the imaginary unit i)?
options: x = 2i and x = -2i
x = 2 and x = -2
x = 4i and x = -4i
x = i and x = -i
questions.explanation: Since x² = -4, taking the square root gives x = ±√(-4) = ±2i, because i² = -1; the equation has no real roots.

questions.text: In how many ways can 3 books be selected from a set of 5 different books, if the order of selection does not matter?
questions.explanation: Selecting 3 items out of 5 without regard to order uses the combination formula ⁵C₃ = 5!/(3!·2!) = 10.

questions.text: What is the coefficient of x² in the binomial expansion of (1 + x)⁴?
questions.explanation: By the binomial theorem, the general term's coefficient for xʳ is ⁴Cᵣ; for r = 2, this is ⁴C₂ = 6.

questions.text: What is the slope of the straight line passing through the points (2, 3) and (6, 11)?
